name: BBC micro:bit v1
summary: The pocket-sized board given to a million UK schoolchildren in 2016: an nRF51822 with Bluetooth LE, 25 LEDs, two buttons and motion sensors.

usb.value: Micro-USB via an NXP KL26Z interface chip

input_voltage.value: 3 V from 2 × AAA batteries or USB

docs.label: micro:bit v1.5 hardware, Micro:bit Educational Foundation

gotchas.title: 16 KB of RAM
gotchas.text: MicroPython programs run out of memory quickly on the v1; larger programs need the v2.

editorial.history: Developed by the BBC with partners and given to UK Year 7 pupils in 2016, the micro:bit was designed so a first program could light its LED grid within minutes.
editorial.today: Still runs MakeCode programs, but new classroom kits ship the v2 with sound and a faster chip.
